chapter_title: Concerning the Summons, in which Limb of the Soul
spiritual_reading:
#
 Spiritual
 Translation


---


**
¶2:**
 The Divine
 Good in its primordial descent extended
 its
 own
 life out
ward,
 distrib
uting the
 faculties of the
 living
 divine
 life
 among separated
 created minds,
 as
 has
 been set
 forth —
 yet
 those
 faculties,
 once
 dispers
ed, did
 not know their
 origin
.
 But
 the Divine
 Itself,
 the
 blessed and glorious source
 of all heav
enly life
, drew
 near inwardly and
 in
 secret:
 according
 to the form of divine truth,
 according
 to the pattern
 of divine good, through
 the sphere of its
 own
 love,
 and
 through
 the pure
 celestial affection of truth proce
eding from itself
 —
 which
 is the inmost life of the Divine
.

---


**¶3:** Consider
 the external
 organization of spiritual life:
 as
 every
 derivative
 faculty
 depends
 upon the governing good of
 the inmost will, so that
 if
 any
 single
 faculty
 should
 be lost
 while
 the ruling
 love endures, restoration
 remains
 possible —
 but
 should
 the
 in
most governing
 good itself
 be destroyed, the entire spiritual life per
ishes and
 is no
 more
.

---

**¶4
:** So
 it
 is with the Divine
 Good in
 its
 descent
:
 it
 is the governing principle,
 and the
 tru
ths and goods that
 proceed from it are
 the derivative
 faculties of
 its
 own life. Or
, in
 another
 lik
eness:
 as
 the universal
 sphere of divine life sust
ains every
 created
 mind, so that
 every
 derived
 intelligence
 exists solely
 by receiving and
 drawing upon
 that
 sphere — so the
 governing
 good is
 established upon the universal
 axis of divine order at
 the
 highest degree of
 the
 created
 universe
.

---

**¶5
:** So
 it is with the Divine:
 it
 is as
 the governing good set
 upon the whole
 organized form of spiritual life, and as
 the universal sust
aining
 sphere established
 in the axis of divine order.
 It
 is made
 powerful
 through
 the pure affection of truth, which
 is its
 own
 inmost life, and which
 it invests with external
 truths as
 with
 a
 garment.

---

**
¶6:** From
 itself
 the Divine brought
 forth and
 sent
 out
ward the successive
 faculties of spiritual perception:
 interior perception, reflective thought, penet
rating understanding, deliberative wisdom, and
 discriminating judgment —
 each
 proce
eding from the one
 will
 and
 dispat
ched
 to accomplish
 the divine
 purpose
. And
 the
 Divine
 Itself followed
 its own proce
eding faculties into lower states.
 For
 its
 living
 life
 was
 ent
angled among the opposing
 falsities and evil affections, as
 though
 those
 scattered
 portions of divine
 life were lim
bs of a
 single body,
 dispers
ed throughout
 the whole
 spiritual
 world
.

---

**¶7
:** And
 when those
 faculties were sent forth
, the
 Divine was
 found united
 with the pure
 celest
ial affection of truth, and it
 arose
,
 seeking
 and
 entre
ating for infl
ux of
 power from
 the in
most.
 And there
 was given
 to it a
 state
 of heav
enly peace
 and conjunction
 through
 love, and the
 perception
 of salvation was
 disclosed
. Then
 the Divine extended
 its own
 faculties and gathered
 the scattered life
 into itself
, and organized
 it in
 its proper
 place as
 a structured form of doctrine and order —
 like
 a containing
 form
 raised
 up
 for
 that
 purpose
.

---

**¶8
:** And it
 shaped
 and perf
ected this
 restored
 form
 with
 consum
mate wisdom
, bringing
 the collected divine
 life into beautiful
 spiritual
 order
. And the tru
ths it
 had
 sent
 forth penet
rated in
ward to
 still
 and
 ext
inguish the burning of self-love
 —
 reaching
 the divine
 life that had
 been crushed and
 oppressed by falsity and evil.
 All
 that
 had
 been scattered
 was gathered in
.
 All that had been displaced
 returned
 and
 was
 established
 firmly
 once more, according to the form
 and
 lik
eness of its
 Divine
 origin.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: Indeed, the First Man dispersed himself and he [gave out every] limb of the living soul as I have written for you [the portions] of the living soul; he has [been cast down and] he did not know [himself nor his origin;] but the blessed, glorious Man came [in] secret; in his image; in his shape; in his love; in his holy virgin, she who is the virgin of light, the soul of the father.

"After the fashion of this fleshly body: as the root of all the limbs hang upon the head, so that should one of the person's limbs be cut off, while the head exists he has hope for [healing;] but if his head should be cut off, the entire body will die and he is lost.

"This is also the case for the Firs[t] Ma[n]. He is the head, while his sons attach to it the limbs [of] his soul. Or, conversely, like the living air, on which all flesh entirely lives as it breathes and [draws life] therein. His head is placed on the body of the Pillar of Glory in the heights of the universe.

"[This i]s also the case [for] the father, the blessed Man; as he is like the head that is upon the body and the air that upon the Pillar is set i[n the heights;] being made strong by his light virgin, [she] who is his soul that he clothes [with garments of light.]

"[From himself he brought forth] t[h]ose [five faculties]: the mind, thought, insight, counsel and c[on]sideration that he produced and sent forth from hi[m to] do his will. He sprang and travelled behind them. [For the sake of the portions] of his living soul, which is entwined among the rebels; as they are like the limbs of its body, and [dispersed throughout the whole] universe.

"And when they were sent, at [that ti]m[e] he was found with the Virgin of [Lig]ht and [he] stood up, asking and entreating for a p[o]wer. [And the Father] gave him peace and a ki[ss of love; and] he [gave] him goo[d] tidings [of the salvation of the] Man. The Man him[s]elf gave [his strength unto] his limbs and gathered his soul i[n to himself; and] he built it in its place like this tower [that is raised up.]

"[And he] shaped it and beautified it skillfully [in its proper] for[m; and] the voices that he sent [forth went inward, so that] he might sink in and quench [the burning of the darkness, and free the] so[u]l that was crushed by the enemy. They were gathered in. They came, set firm once more, in the image of their father."
